w4oeha:289: Traditional kernel development requires engineers to simultaneously master three layers of knowledge: hardware architecture constraints (partition dimensions, memory hierarchy), the programming model (NKI API semantics), and performance engineering (profiling + optimization loops). The intersection of these three layers of knowledge is extremely small, making engineers who can write high-performance kernels scarce. The core insight of Neuron Agentic Development is to encode these three layers of knowledge as Agent Skills—hardware constraints are embedded in the tiling strategy of the writing skill, API semantics are encoded in the docs skill, and performance engineering is formalized as a combination of profiling + querying skills. This allows ML engineers to focus on "what I want to implement" rather than "how the hardware constrains me."
